fieldMarks: Male dark slaty gray with a yellow comb and a long blackish tail tipped with a broad pale gray band
In spring display the male shows yellow neck air sacs ringed by white feathers
Large: Alaska's largest upland game bird
behavior: Displaying males give deep, owl-like hoots, often from high in a dense conifer, sometimes audible over a mile away
Forages on the ground in summer and in trees in winter, eating conifer needles
Hens with broods use muskeg edges, logged areas and roadsides from late June
habitat: Coastal and mountain coniferous forest; many birds move in autumn from open breeding areas into dense conifers; coastal birds may use semi-open old-growth or logged forest year-round.
range: Resident from coastal southeastern Alaska and coastal British Columbia (including Haida Gwaii and Vancouver Island) south through the coast ranges and Cascades to northwestern California and the Sierra Nevada.

lookalikes.name: Dusky grouse
lookalikes.howToTell: Very similar and separated mainly by range; dusky grouse lives in the interior West.
